signal: D-Tools released System Integrator v24 in April 2026 with AI-powered tools and multi-user editing, showcased at InfoComm 2026.

email.body1:
Jeff, saw D-Tools shipped SI v24 with AI tools and multi-user editing, then showcased it at InfoComm.

A major release usually surfaces more system integrators in play than the SI team can cover before interest fades, and that gap is where deals stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for D-Tools off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jeff, quick follow-up for D-Tools.

After a release and a big show, the SI target list grows faster than the team can touch. Most leaders don't actually know how many meetings each rep needs to convert that interest, so the gap surfaces late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings D-Tools needs to keep the SI funnel covered without hiring more reps.
email.body3:
Jeff, last bit of proof for D-Tools.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how D-Tools' reply rate likely compares to similar B2B software teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jeff, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling SI coverage without adding reps isn't a priority post-launch, no problem at all. A release-plus-tradeshow quarter is its own kind of busy, and timing matters most here.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your SI motion? I'll tailor it to D-Tools either way.
